title: PHARM · Allopurinol (MAKE LESS) vs colchicine (CALM THE FLARE): body explainer

belief: Allopurinol stops a gout attack, and it should be stopped during a flare.

steps.line: Too much uric acid forms crystals
steps.sub: Needle crystals in a joint, often the big toe

steps.line: White cells attack the crystals: a flare

steps.line: Allopurinol: the liver makes less uric acid
steps.sub: Prevention over months. Not for tonight's pain
steps.shown: the aqua capsule docks on the liver's uric acid machine (xanthine oxidase); fewer dots leave; a months counter; crystals shrink slowly; the pain meter stays high; stamp MAKE LESS

steps.sub: Treats the flare. Start it early

allopurinol: Blocks xanthine oxidase: the body makes less uric acid; crystals dissolve over months (prevention, not flare pain relief)
Keep taking it during a flare (allopurinol label counseling); flare prophylaxis (low-dose colchicine or an NSAID) for 3 to 6 months when starting (ACR 2020)
Any rash: hold it and notify the prescriber right away (label: discontinue permanently at the first rash; SJS, TEN, DRESS)
colchicine: Calms the white cells at the crystals (stops neutrophil activation and migration): treats the flare, not a painkiller, does not lower uric acid
Start at the first sign of a flare (label); most effective within about 12 to 24 hours (MSD Manual); low dose as ordered
Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, muscle pain or weakness can herald toxicity: hold it and report; interactions (strong CYP3A4, P-gp inhibitors, grapefruit), kidneys and liver

choice.question: Gout flare, already on allopurinol. Stop it?
choice.b: Keep allopurinol, colchicine for the flare

memory_line: Allopurinol makes less. Colchicine calms the flare.
caption_lesson:
🦶 First, what a gout flare is
• Too much uric acid in the blood forms needle-shaped crystals in a joint, often the big toe
• White blood cells attack the crystals: red, hot, swollen, very painful

🩵 Allopurinol (MAKE LESS)
• Blocks the enzyme that makes uric acid (xanthine oxidase), so the body makes less
• Prevention: crystals dissolve over months. It doesn't stop tonight's pain
• Keep taking it during a flare. Starting it can trigger flares at first, so low-dose colchicine or an NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug) is usually given with it for 3 to 6 months
• Drink enough fluid for at least 2 L (liters) of urine a day
• Any rash: hold it and tell the prescriber right away. It can be the first sign of a severe skin or whole-body reaction
• Southeast Asian or African American descent? Ask about the HLA-B*5801 gene test before it starts

💜 Colchicine (CALM THE FLARE)
• Calms the white cells attacking the crystals, so the flare settles. Not a painkiller, and it doesn't lower uric acid
• Start it at the first sign of a flare, low dose as ordered
• Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, or muscle pain or weakness can be early toxicity: hold it and report
• Avoid grapefruit. Check other meds, the kidneys and the liver

✅ The right move
• Flare on allopurinol: keep it going, treat the flare as ordered
• Allopurinol rash: hold it, report right away
• Colchicine GI (stomach and bowel) symptoms: hold it, report
